Phenylbutyric Acid is known to be involved in the pathogenesis of Neonatal Intrahepatic Cholestasis Due To Citrin Deficiency, suggesting a possible role in the metabolic dysfunction of this condition. The high scores in both paths indicate a strong, consistent relationship, likely due to the shared involvement of Phenylbutyric Acid in the metabolic cascade. The evidence supports a mechanistic link where Glycerol Phenylbutyrate may influence the metabolic pathway leading to the development of the condition. However, the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated, and further research is needed to confirm the therapeutic potential of Glycerol Phenylbutyrate in this context.
